Description: On January 23, 2009 I worked the 330‐1130 shift in full uniform assigned as system wide coverage for the Explosive Detection Unit in an unmarked Fo Police Plate 121. Coming up behind with lights still activated the car made no attempt to stop for approximately the next ½ mile. Finally the ca slowed and appeared to be stopping only to speed up and continue on. I activated the siren now without any response. The Impala got off at exit 14 r of the ramp and stopped at the red light. I pulled the cruiser to the left of this car and angled it front of this car partially blocking its path. No soon approach, the car sped off through the intersection. It pulled into the Home Depot Parking lot and turned around coming at me on my left. I stopped confronted the operator and only occupant; the drivers window now down. I demanded his license and registration. He yelled in response who are yo and again demanded his paperwork. What police? he argued. The Transit Police I replied. I asked a third time for his license and registration and inform subject to arrest if he did not comply. With this the operator put the car in drive and began to slowly pull away. I reached in grabbed his left hand and window. I now had the subject in a wrist lock and at the same time order him to place the car in park. He told me I was in trouble now and to keep it to do" as he would sue me civillialy. It wasn't until I applied pressure on the wrist lock as a pain compliance technique did the subject put the car in pa and registration again he yelled "where are we now" in apparent reference to my jurisdiction. I physically took him out of the car with the wrist lock a Boston Police cavalierly badge fell from his vest pocket. Asked if he was a P.O. he responded, "Keep it up kid. Do what you have to do I'll sue you." A p weapons on him. I retrieved a Ma. license and Boston Police Id card from his right front pocket identifying him as Detective Robert Tully of Hanover, M weapons and he stated his department Glock was in the bag. After turning the ignition off and removing the keys, I checked the compartment area fo Tully in the passenger seat out of the elements. His department firearm was located in the trunk which I kept for safe keeping. I then removed the ha wait in his car. While conversing with Mr. Tully I now detected an aroma of alcohol on his breath. I notified duty supervisor, Sgt. Cantella of the situate supervisor from our agency as well as Boston Police to take charge of Mr. Tully, his department cruiser and firearm. Sgt. Roy responded to assist. Sgt Lt. Lanchester of C‐11 was apprised of the situation. BPD. Officers Giannetti, Fogerty and Sgt. Brennan all from C‐11 responded. During this time, Mr. wait had to take a bathroom break before this encounter was over. I issued Mr. Tully two citations #'s M1803359 & M1803360 for following too close reckless operation and refusal to submit, both criminal complaints issued in hand. Mr. Tully, his weapon and cruiser were turned over to Sgt. Brennan and I cleared the scene.

At about 17:11 hours on January 29, 2020 while assigned to the Bureau of Field Services, Night Command, I received a telephone call from Superinten Superintendent Eddings informed me that a complaint had been received regarding a Detail Officer at Congress St/ Atlantic Ave. directing traffic while Superintendent Eddings further directed me to identify the oﬃcer, determine if the complaint was correct, and if so to initiate a BlueTeam Complaint Using the BlueNote Detail system I identified the officer assigned to that location as PO Shayna Rivera, ID# 144503, assigned to District 1. The Detail Properties, 280 Congress St. I responded to that location and observed PO Rivera directing traffic in front of the garage exit. PO Rivera was wearing a jacket yellow side out, uniform pants, and white sneakers. I spoke to PO Rivera and inquired about the white sneakers. She exclaimed “Oh My God, was running late to the detail because of an arrest, I was in the K‐Car, and when I got here, I forgot to put on my black shoes! They are in my car right on.” PO Rivera then walked over to her personal vehicle which was parked at the curb, pulled black shoes out of the trunk and put them on. PO Rivera was in violation of Rule 306, Section 6, which species in relevant part: Shoes: ?Low quarter, military style, black shoes of smooth leather or Corfam, with plain toes and laces; … Utilizing Rule 109, Section 5, I admonished PO Rivera to not forget in the future, and she assured me that the issue would not reoccur. Rule 109 Section 6 reads in relevant part:Sec. 6 Oral Reprimands: Oral reprimands, given by supervisors for minor violations of the Rules and Procedu uniform or reporting late for duty, are simply spoken censures or reproofs. While a notation that an oral reprimand was given is entered into the list record, no record of the reprimand goes into the permanent personnel file. The rule contemplates that such reprimands will be given on an informal prior notice. In conformance with my instructions from Superintendent Eddings, this Oral Reprimand is being entered in to the BlueTeam Systemin order to memo

Description: On Sunday, December 29, 2019 at about 10:39 AM I interviewed Henry Herman Reid‐Morrison who responded to Area B‐2 to make a complain Boston P.O.s assaulting him the previous evening at Intervale St and Fernboro St. Mr. Reid‐ Morrison stated that he was operating a Mazda fou sedan (owned by his friend Carl Jean‐Louis) and stopped at Intervale St and Fernboro to drop his friend /witness Marcus Eddins off at his home at 26 Fernboro St apartment 3 Dorchester #857‐415‐8367. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that he was approached by three P.O.s when he exited th Mazda, Mr. Eddins was still seated in the motor vehicle. The P.O.s told him he looked suspicious and that he looked like he was urinating on the sidewalk. Mr. Reid‐Morrison denies urinating. Mr. Reid‐Morrison admits that he and Mr. Eddins were at Club Saavor earlier in the night and had drinking. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that he remembers being on the ground handcuffed being kicked in the face. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that doesn't remember what happened from the initial encounter with the police to being on the ground handcuffed. When asked Mr. Reid‐Morriso admits that he may of gotten mouthy with the officers because he didn't like being stopped or his motor vehicle being searched. Mr. Reid‐Morr stated that police didn't find anything in his motor vehicle, but threatened to arrest him. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated he asked the police why the him up, and the police told him he scratched himself on the ground. Mr. Reid‐ Morrison stated he was bleeding from the nose, un‐handcuffed a released. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that the police took his identification but is un‐aware if the police wrote down his information. Mr. Reid‐Mo stated that he asked for the others names and he was denied that information. Mr. Reid‐Morrison describes the officers as‐ three white males, plain clothes, one of the officers had facial hair and was wearing a red hoodie. N hair on the other two officers. All appeared to be in their early thirties. When asked Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that the officers said they were p but he didn't see any badges or rearms with them. He has no idea what kind of vehicle they were operating. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that another officer arrived when he was in handcuffs. He describes this officer as a white male, in his thirties, and in Boston Police uniform. Mr. Reid‐Morrison stated that this over was not involved just there. I asked Mr. Reid‐Morrison if there was anything else he wanted to add or is there something I'm not asking him and he stated no. I observed Mr. Reid‐Morrison to be holding an ice pack to the right side of his face which appeared to be swollen, he had a swollen lip with discoloration on the inside, and he complains of pain to the right rear of his head, and a swollen nose. I asked Mr. Reid‐Morrison if he wanted m attention and he declined. Mr. Reid‐Morrison showed me a photograph of himself on his cell phone time stamped on today date at 2:41 AM, it showed him with a bloody blood on his lips, blood on his left eye, and a swollen right cheek. Mr. Reid‐Morrison also showed me a video of himself which he stated was just the incident where he is complaining of what happened to him using profanities. I took a photograph on my department phone of the photogram I recorded the video on my department phone as well. Mr. Reid‐Morrison was checked for outstanding warrants, not finding any Mr. Reid‐Mor left District B‐2.

This complaint is regarding the two P.O.s that were stationed at the Boston polling location at Woodbourne Apartments (6 Southbourne Road, Plain, MA 02130) during the last election on the morning of Tuesday, September 24, 2019 (approx. 6am‐1pm). I was serving as a poll worker for precinct 19‐12. Precinct 19‐7 was also present at the polling location. I was extremely disappointed to see the behavior of the two police offers at the polling location in the morning. The officers were supposed to be checking residents out, but they were completely inattentive and seem had no interest in doing the job. One of the offers was watching a movie on his phone for the entire morning. He had earphones in and had no awareness of residents coming up to the desk to be checked out. He didn't bother to remove the earphones and hardly even looked up when residents approached the desk. The other officer was talking on the phone (on personal calls) for half the morning. When residents approached desk to be checked out, they were confused as to whether he was talking to them or not. He didn't bother to put the phone calls on hold when needed help. In my opinion, the unprofessional behavior of both officers was completely unacceptable and may have affected the accuracy of t check‐out logs. I sincerely hope that I don't see the same behavior during the next election on November 5. Unfortunately, I do not know the n the officers or the badge numbers, but they said they were from District A‐1.

The incident of note occurred August 31, 2019 in Boston, MA. The agency involved was the Boston Police Dept. I am 64 years of age, and currently live in the North‐East Kingdom (NEK) of Vermont. I require the use of one or two "Canadian Cane" style cut mobility due to neurological damage I received roughly 23 years ago. I also have damage to multiple discs in my neck and back, as confirmed by MRIs. I was a participant in the counter‐protest at the Government Center on August 31. I was using a single crutch for mobility because I was carrying "street‐medic" bag. When the BPD Bicycle Unit attacked protesters, I was one of the people knocked down. In falling, I lost my grip on my crutch arrested anyone that fell. An officer, believed to be Capt Danilecki of the Bicycle Unit, then sprayed a large amount of pepper‐spray or mace in eyes. During my arrest, a bearded officer took my crutch and carried it away, despite my repeated insistence that I am disabled and need the cr move. Another over took my medic‐bag that had my cellphone inside. None of these items were booked with me at A1 Precinct. On Sept. 3, 2019, I returned to Boston for court, where all legal charges against me were dropped. I went over to the A1 Precinct, where I was b and filed a request for information regarding the disposition of my missing items.To date, my Canadian Cane has not been returned, nor has th responded in any way. The medic‐bag and cellphone are also still missing. Several videos from the protest are available; that show me treating for pepper‐spray; that show the bearded officer walking away with my crutch; and that show another officer picking up my medic‐bag. So there video evidence available showing that all my items, especially the crutch, were in BPD control. There all also videos documenting an officer half dragging me away and it is obvious just how much pain I was in. I repeatedly noticed others of my disabilities but they were completely ignored I wish to ale and proceed with an ADA complaint against the Boston Police Department and the City of Boston.

No one ended up coming. The two officers told me that they "were going to beat my ass." It g the point where I had to make space between them and I because I felt as if they were actually going to assault me or unjustly arrest me. Later night, I went to the District A‐1 office to file a complaint/police report. I was told that I "had mental health problems" by Officer McCarthy who manning down the front desk. Officers refused to file a complaint or report on those two officers. I would not leave from the District A‐1 office was actually taking seriously, however, they never did. I ended up waiting in the station for 3 and a half hours. The whole time I was at the from waiting while it sat vacant for those 3 and a half which I assume is not protocol or the right thing to do. Officer McCarthy also called an ambulant get me out of the police station as if I was extremely intoxicated. I was not. The ambulance came and they did tests on me then told Officer Mc that I was not extremely intoxicated and told him that they could not do anything. I ended up leaving around 7:30 as I did not sleep because I w dealing with this situation. All of this happened last night because the cops were called on me. I am unable to find my phone at the moment and will be getting one soon, so email would probably work best to communicate.

About 1600 hours on Sunday, June 9, 2019, Capt. McCormick was contacted by A‐7 supervisors Wilbanks and Hurely, stating that Officer Maria 112887) was missing her firearm. Capt. McCormick responded to A‐7 and spoke with Lt. Wilbanks, Sgt. Hurley and Officer. Larry Calderon (unio representitive). It was Officr King's statement that after a First half on Saturday, June 8th, she left work and went to Jevelli's restaurant at 387 C St to meet up with co‐workers. She states she has a specific memory of securing her firearm in the glove compartment of her POV and that she locked the glove compartment. She then entered Jevelli's, leaving at about 2AM. She then proceeded to park her car on Orleans St by the Cuna Tavern, and then stayed the night at a friend's apartment (S. Wilbanks). On Sunday, at about 1130 hours, she returned to her car and realized h firearm was missing. She states that she searched the car as well as the apartment, and was assisted in re‐searching it by Wilbanks and Caldero they had no success, they immediately reported to District 7 to advise the Duty Supervisor. I was contacted by Lt. Wilbanks as well and respond 7 to begin investigation. All A‐7 officers avaiable, including detectives, were assigned to last known possible locations of firearm to continue to se K‐9 capable of searching for firearms was brought in to assist to no avail. Internal Affairs was notified (McCOrmick) and Lt. Det. Troy as well as S Detectives McCarthy and Miller responded. Sgt. Det. Duggan took over initial investigation and asked certain questions of Officer King. Officer K made certain statements and then invoked her right to remain silent. Deputy McGolderick was notified (McCormick), and Officer King was admit she would be placed on Administrative Duty until otherwise notified. Sgt. Det. Duggan maintained control of the investigation and ordered avail detectives to go recover any and all videos available from any locations near where any events may have happened. District level investigation continues until BIS makes determination of next steps. At this point of the investigation, an off‐duty officer has lost control of a department issued, fully loaded firearm. At the least, this amounts to n duty and potentially a failure to properly secure a department firearm. Invesitgation continues.

I was illegally towed on Wednesday, June 5th. I was parked on the odd (south) side of the street on Temple Pl, in downtown Boston, where you park from 7 p.m. to 7 a.m., as I have many times before. My car had been towed before I went outside before 7 a.m. that morning. On the BPD inventory page, the officer wrote the address for my car as 52 Temple Place, which would be the even (north) side of the street. The entire eve (north) side of the street on Temple Place is a No Parking zone, and therefore, I was unable to win the hearing I had with the Parking Clerk to re towing fees and to fight the parking ticket. I do not understand how an officer can put a completely incorrect address for the location of a park especially in this instance, when my car was parked about half way down the street and on the opposite side from where he said it was. The far my evidence said 52 Temple Pl. meant I could never win the dispute I had for the towing, which I would have most certainly won had the locate parked car been accurately reported.

As I was walking to the commuter rail station, I noticed a BPD cruiser pulling out from the village market parking lot in the wrong direction. I did notice any signalling on their part as they reversed in to a parking spot. As I walked by, I stopped and asked if they would pull someone over wh the same thing they did. They said their lights were on, I said I didn't see them and was then told by the passenger that I should buy some sung When I asked why they needed to cut through the parking lot instead of going around (like everyone is supposed to), I was told to mind my own business. As someone who has 15 years of customer service and working with troubled teens, I'm wondering how your officers are trained to respond to questions from the public. Furthermore, who is assigning traffic duty? BPD is nowhere to be found in Rozzie Village from 8am until 9am, but then they show up at 930 on to police a crosswalk where most folks actually stop and a supermarket exit? That's a waste of resources. Anyways, I'd love to know about the type of de‐escalation training officers receive as well as training with the general public. When I ask a quest an oﬃcer, as a taxpayer and a resident of Boston I expect to be treated with respect by the employees of the city.

On Friday, May 10, 2019 Ms. Crystal Depina entered Schroeder Pl. in an effort to obtain a copy of her 16 yr old daughter's arrest report (I# 1920 from a domestic violence incident that had occurred on April 30, 2019. When Ms. Depina was not provided with a copy of the confidential rep asked to speak with an IIU investigator. S/D Lembo then spoke with Ms. Depina in the lobby. She provided that in addition to not being given a the report she wanted to complain that the officers must have lied in their report, even though she did not know the contents of the report. Sh advised to obtain the report from her daughter's attorney, review it and contact this officer if she needed additional assistance. About 1:30 PM Monday, May 13, 2019 Ms. Depina returned to Schroeder Plaza in an effort to show this investigator video from the incident. Ms Depina was e to the IIU offices and interviewed by S/D Pusey and S/D Lembo. Ms. Depina commented that she believes that the arresting officers used excess force while placing her daughter in custody. She showed two (2) video segments that show the officers in a doorway attempting to secure her daughter. She also showed a number of still images depicting bruising to her daughter's chest, arms and face. The facial bruising was received the reported domestic incident not as a result of the arrest. Ms. Depina provided that her daughter has emotional and psychological issues and from seizures. Ms. Depina has forwarded the still images and a partial video this investigator.

Camera footage later revealed that the bus attempted to pull to the right required by law, but could not due to the presence of another motor vehicle on his right. Officer Geary was assigned as the "rifle car" and was operating a Patrol Supervisor motor vehicle due to the fact that the assigned gun car was in the shop for repairs. At some point as Officer Gea attempted to squeeze by the bus, he came into contact with the side of the bus, causing slight damage to bus and slight damage to side of cruise Officer Geary stopped quickly, but then continued to call to assist. After the initial events, Officer Geary failed to report the accident to a super and follow the usual procedures for reporting and documenting a Department motor vehicle accident. Sgt. Harrington was assigned to research events and was able to ascertain that Officer Geary did in fact come in contact with the bus (bus driver report CC#19202786 and other supply and was also able to retrieve video from bus cameras. Officer Geary failed to timely report such, going on Dyas off and then Military Days, befog ordered back to work to report. He was advised of his Canrey and Weingartn rights for precautionary reasons. Rule 102 Section 4. states 4 NEGLECT OF DUTY: This includes any conduct or omission which is not in accordance with established and ordinary or procedures as to such employees or which constitutes use of unreasonable judgment in the exercising of any discretion granted to an employee. The ordinary and proper procedure for officers involved in a motor vehicle accident is to immediately report and document such (Rule 316). Of Geary neglected to do such, and in doing so, violated Rule 102 Section 4. Upon having conversation with Officer Geary about the circumstances nervous and embarrassed about the events, he was forthright and accepting of the situation and understood the nature and necessity of the Ru Regulations. He understands and accepts responsibility for the events and understands and is not resistant to the fact that disciplinary action m necessary.

A detail that was located at 542 Dorch time of 8:00 AM. A short time later Officer Vasquez became aware of his mistake and went to the detail at 510 Dorchester Ave. On his Burns was working the detail. I learned Sgt. Burns was working the detail because he was assigned a Bond Bros detail at 515 E 1ST in Burns arrived at that location the crew was not there. Sgt. Burns contacted the Bond Bros supervisor who was at 510 Dorchester Ave. asked Sgt. Burns to come to 510 Dorchester because he did not have a detail. Officer Vasquez and Sgt. Burns were now at the same d Vasquez was properly assigned the detail they decided Sgt. Burns would stay at the detail. Sgt. Burns did call for the detail supervisor rectify the situation. Officer Vasquez had the Bond Bros supervisor sign him out of the detail at 10:30 AM for a minimum of four hours another construction company working in the area (Trinity Green Construction) and inquired if they had a detail. Officer Vasquez learn detail and called the Area C detail room and spoke to Officer Blicker to order a detail for this company. Trinity Green Construction did was from 7:00 AM to 11:00 AM. When Officer Vasquez spoke to the detail room it was after 11:00 AM and Trinity Green was almost d doing. Officer Blicker never spoke to the supervisor of Trinity Green Construction to verify he needed or wanted a detail anymore and what time. When Trinity Green Construction completed the work they were conducting, Officer Vasquez gave the supervisor a detail card with th detail was from 11:15 AM to 4:00 PM. On further investigation I spoke to the Trinity Green supervisor Mr. Thomas Miller who stated h detail room to confirm with them he needed a detail after 11:00 AM and for how long he would need the detail. Mr. Miller stated the was complete by 12:30 PM and Oﬃcer Vasquez handed him the detail card to sign with the hours already called out. About 2:30 PM Sgt. Mylett went to the Trinity Green detail to speak to Officer Vasquez but he was not there. Sgt. Mylett attempted to radio but he did not answer. As a result of my investigation I did not find Officer Vasquez violated any criminal law. I did find Officer Vasquez was in violation of Bo and Procedures specifically Rule 325 Paid Details Sec 2 (approaching the Trinity Green Construction to hire a detail), Sec 7 (submitting not actually worked) and working in excess of 18 hours by working 18.5 hours on June 3, 2016 a violation of the 18 hour rule. I also fin is in violation of Rule 325 Paid Details Sec 3 by not speaking to the vendor to authorize a second detail created for Trinity Green Const
